Learning by insight is based on previous experience that is suddenly pieced together in the mind.

A sudden connection of relationships or components to an answer comes together and the solution appears.

When insight occurs, the learner has made many connections between different concepts.The final link which brings the person to a solution happens after the person quietly ponders a number of different possibilities.�

For example, you may slave over a math equations for several minutes. Then you take a closer look at something you have scribbled beside the equations as a possible solution. Your doodles cause you to take your thinking one step beyond your current stage of thinking and the correct answer falls into place.

In�pop culture, learning by insight is referred to as a�Eureka�moment or an�Aha! Moment. �
